title: Prompt OpenAI Models with Evaluated Contracts
summary: Design clear, versioned prompts for ChatGPT and API workflows, separate instruction authority from variable input, and improve behavior with controlled evaluations.
objectives: Define success criteria and representative evaluation cases before tuning a prompt.
Structure goals, authoritative instructions, context, examples, variable input, output contracts, and verification.
Adapt prompting to the selected model and surface without hard-coding volatile guidance.
Classify failures across prompt, context, model, tool, policy, and application boundaries.

sections.title: Start from success evidence
paragraphs: Write the required outcome, target users, unacceptable behavior, output contract, representative cases, rubric, and pass threshold before changing prompt wording. Compare candidates against the same cases and configuration.
Prompt engineering cannot repair unavailable facts, missing permissions, a broken tool, unsuitable latency, or absent application validation. Classify the failed boundary before editing.
sections.callout: A response that sounds better is not evidence of a better prompt.

code.label: Success criteria and cases before prompt changes

sections.title: State the contract clearly and once
paragraphs: Describe the outcome, audience, authoritative context, hard constraints, allowed actions, approval boundaries, required evidence, output shape, and stopping condition. Use ordered steps only when order or completeness is a real requirement.
Avoid duplicated or conflicting instructions. Keep stable policy in the appropriate higher-authority instruction layer and put task-specific requests in the user input.

code.label: Stable policy in instructions, task in input

sections.title: Separate context, examples, and untrusted input
paragraphs: Label authoritative references, examples, and variable user or retrieved content. Use clear delimiters or structured fields, and tell the workflow which evidence may support claims.
Prompt structure does not create security. Treat external text as untrusted data, enforce authorization outside the model, validate outputs, and never include secrets merely to make them available.

code.label: Evaluated prompt contract
code.code:
Goal: [OBSERVABLE OUTCOME]
Authoritative instructions: [POLICY + HARD CONSTRAINTS]
Trusted context: [APPROVED SOURCES]
Variable input (untrusted): [USER OR RETRIEVED DATA]
Examples: [RELEVANT, DIVERSE, SECRET-FREE]
Output contract: [SCHEMA OR REQUIRED HEADINGS]
Verify: [CLAIMS, CONSTRAINTS, POSTCONDITIONS]
Stop or escalate when: [BOUNDARY]

sections.title: Adapt with current model guidance
paragraphs: Model families can differ in reasoning controls, verbosity, tool behavior, and recommended prompt patterns. Use the current official model guidance for the configured model and evaluate changes rather than copying a static recipe.
Keep model identifiers and model-specific settings in reviewed configuration. Change one meaningful hypothesis at a time where practical and preserve the baseline for rollback.

code.label: Model-specific settings as reviewed configuration

sections.title: Iterate and version from evidence
paragraphs: Run baseline and candidate across typical, edge, adversarial, and prior-failure cases. Record per-case rubric results, critical failures, latency, usage, cost, model, prompt, tools, and reviewer disagreement.

Classify each miss as instruction ambiguity, missing context, misleading example, output violation, model limitation, tool failure, policy boundary, or application defect. Add repaired failures to regression coverage.

code.label: Promote a prompt version only on measured evidence

activity.title: Build and evaluate an OpenAI prompt contract
instructions: Choose a recurring task and define at least four success criteria, one forbidden outcome, and an 80 percent pass threshold.
Create six cases: three typical, one edge, one adversarial instruction-conflict case, and one prior failure.
Write a prompt that separates authoritative instructions, trusted context, untrusted variable input, examples, output contract, verification, and escalation.
Compare a baseline and candidate under identical settings, classify every failure boundary, and make a ship, revise, or reject decision.
evidence: A secret-free versioned prompt, rubric, and six-case suite with explicit trust and approval boundaries.
A baseline-versus-candidate report with scores, failures, versions, latency and usage evidence, and a release decision.
activity.reflectionPrompt: Which failed case required a system change rather than another prompt instruction?

Allow three minutes to classify one miss as prompt, context, model, tool, policy, or application failure.

Begin the check after the learner can improve behavior from evidence without treating every failure as wording.

questions.prompt: What should exist before prompt tuning?
choices: Success criteria, cases, rubric, and threshold
In the appropriate higher-authority instruction layer
questions.explanation: Instruction authority should match the policy's ownership and stability.

choices: Clearer structure, not trust or enforcement
questions.explanation: External systems must enforce security, authority, and validation.

questions.prompt: How should model-specific guidance be applied?
choices: Verify current official guidance and evaluate it on the configured model
questions.explanation: Model behavior and recommendations change and require controlled evaluation.

questions.prompt: A result lacks data the workflow never supplied. What failed first?
questions.explanation: Prompt wording cannot recover authoritative data that is unavailable.
